title: Senior Director, Brand Governance & Creative Systems
description: As Senior Director, Brand Governance & Creative Systems reporting to the AVP, Creative & Brand Design, you'll play a critical role in protecting, scaling, and operationalizing Nasdaq's brand across teams, channels, and regions. Senior Director, Brand Governance & Creative Systems As Senior Director, Brand Governance & Creative Systems reporting to the AVP, Creative & Brand Design, you'll play a critical role in protecting, scaling, and operationalizing Nasdaq's brand across teams, channels, and regions. You'll lead the brand and design governance frameworks, creative standards, and systems that enable consistent, high-quality brand expression — while driving responsible adoption of AI and emerging creative technologies. You'll thrive in this position if you're a strategic, systems-oriented leader who brings deep expertise in brand and design, strong operational instincts, and a passion for enabling teams to create with confidence and consistency. Key Responsibilities Lead the development and evolution of enterprise brand standards, governance frameworks, and creative operating models — including review, approval, escalation, and exception workflows that balance creative flexibility with consistency. Define and uphold creative and design standards across visual identity, typography, imagery, motion, digital experiences, templates, and other brand applications, ensuring accessible and inclusive design across all workflows. Lead the enterprise strategy for responsible AI adoption and creative technology governance, establishing policies, standards, approved workflows, and oversight frameworks for generative AI and AI-assisted creative work. Govern the enterprise creative technology ecosystem — including platforms such as Adobe Creative Cloud, Adobe Express, Canva, and Figma — evaluating new tools based on creative value, brand impact, risk, and scalability. Build scalable systems for enterprise templates, design systems, asset lifecycle management, metadata, taxonomy, and distribution of approved creative resources across the organization. Lead enterprise education and change-management programs for brand standards, AI, and creative technologies, establishing KPIs to measure brand compliance, tool adoption, and operational effectiveness. Lead brand governance for M&A integration, naming, product taxonomy, sub-brand architecture, partnerships, and third-party brand usage. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Design, Marketing, Communications, Business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. 10+ years of experience in brand, design, creative operations, or brand governance, with 5+ years leading teams, programs, or enterprise-scale initiatives. Deep understanding of brand identity, visual design systems, and contemporary creative best practices, with demonstrated experience developing governance frameworks and approval models. Experience evaluating, implementing, or governing enterprise creative technologies and AI-enabled workflows, including strong knowledge of generative AI opportunities and associated risks. Strong project, program, and stakeholder management skills with experience operating in complex, globally matrixed organizations. Excellent communication and presentation skills with a track record of driving organizational change and adoption across diverse audiences. Preferred Qualifications Experience within financial services, technology, B2B, or regulated industries. Knowledge of intellectual property, trademark, rights management, and brand protection practices. Experience with enterprise creative technology ecosystems, DAM platforms, workflow automation, AI governance policies, and content operations. Come as You Are Nasdaq is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and identities. We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where diverse perspectives, experiences, and identities are valued and celebrated. We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodation throughout the hiring process. What We Offer We’re proud to offer a competitive rewards package that is meaningful, recognizes the unique needs of our employees and their families and incentivizes employees for their contribution to Nasdaq’s overall success. The base pay range for this role is $129,000 - $239,000. In addition to base salary, Nasdaq provides a generous annual bonus/commission (short-term incentive), and equity (long-term incentive), comprehensive benefits, and opportunity for growth. Exact compensation may vary based on several job-related factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to: skill set, experience, education/training, business needs and market demands. title: AI Security Governance Principal
description: About Invesco As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco. What’s in it for you? Our people are at the ver y core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our comprehensive compensation and benefit offerings including: Flexible paid time off Hybrid work schedule 401(K) matching of 100% up to the first 6% with a discretionary supplemental contribution Health & wellbeing benefits Parental Leave benefits Employee stock purchase plan Job Description Your Role We are seeking an experienced AI Security Governance Lead – Principal to establish and operate the AI security governance capability as a hands-on individual contributor. The role combines governance leadership with direct analyst execution, including AI use-case intake, inventory management, risk assessments, architecture and control reviews, governance documentation, evidence collection, issue tracking, metrics, and committee support. The individual will build structure in an evolving environment, independently manage the day-to-day workload, and influence decisions across all levels of the organization. You Will Be Responsible For: Governance Operations and Delive ry Own and operate the end-to-end AI security governance workflow, from use-case intake and risk classification through review, approval, remediation, deployment, periodic reassessment, and retirement. Create and maintain the enterprise inventory of AI use cases, models, agents, platforms, vendors, owners, data classifications, deployment environments, approval status, and residual risks. Configure and administer intake forms, risk questionnaires, decision criteria, approval workflows, risk registers, exception records, and remediation trackers using Jira, Confluence, GRC platforms, or similar tools. Manage the daily review queue, prioritize requests based on risk and business need, monitor service levels, and follow up directly with stakeholders to resolve gaps and overdue actions. Lead security deliverables within the AI Foundations program from requirements definition through implementation and operationalization, including roadmaps, milestones, procedures, metrics, and sustainable ownership. AI Model Risk Review Perform AI security and risk assessments in alignment with the enterprise model risk framework, and automate repeatable portions of the assessment process where practical. Assess foundation models, local large language models, AI agents, AI platforms, retrieval-augmented generation solutions, and third-party AI services across their lifecycle. Review solution architectures, data flows, prompts, integrations, identities, permissions, APIs, plugins, tool access, logging, monitoring, and agent actions to identify security and control weaknesses. Execute structured control reviews and coordinate specialized testing for prompt injection, sensitive data exposure, insecure output handling, excessive agency, hallucination, jailbreaking, supply-chain compromise, bias, and misalignment. Define security requirements and compensating controls for AI systems of all types and levels of criticality; document findings, risk decisions, exceptions, control owners, and residual risk. Shadow AI Risk Management Establish and operate controls for detecting, assessing, and governing shadow AI, including unauthorized models, applications, browser services, plugins, agents, and developer tools. Analyze outputs from AI discovery, data loss prevention, cloud access security broker, SaaS security, cloud security, identity, and monitoring tools to identify unmanaged AI usage and prioritize investigation. Define and maintain governance and security requirements for Model Context Protocol usage, including detection, restriction, approval, authentication, authorization, logging, and exception processes. Investigate identified use cases, document risk and business context, recommend approved alternatives or compensating controls, and track remediation through closure. Produce recurring dashboards that provide leadership with visibility into AI adoption, unauthorized usage, review volumes, aging actions, exceptions, control effectiveness, and material risk trends. Threat and Regulatory Monitoring Monitor the evolving AI threat landscape, including offensive AI use, AI supply-chain risks, and attacks against AI-enabled applications provided by critical suppliers. Assess the relevance and potential impact of emerging threats; document findings and update controls, standards, questionnaires, and monitoring requirements accordingly. title: Internal Auditor - Technology Audit
description: To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts. Job Category Finance Job Details About Salesforce Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all. Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce. The Experience The Internal Audit Organization is an independent and objective function that assists Salesforce to meet its goals through independent reviews and assessments. Specifically, the Internal Audit Organization evaluates and provides recommendations to enhance the effectiveness, efficiency, and scalability of the company’s processes, information systems, and underlying internal control environment. The Internal Audit Organization also evaluates and assists in improving the effectiveness of the Company’s risk management and governance processes. This function reports administratively to the President and Chief Operating and Financial Officer (COFO) and directly to the Audit and Finance Committee of the Company’s Board of Directors. Internal Audit is modernizing the way we perform our audits, using technology, AI, and analytics to fuel the transformation. We are looking for an Internal Auditor to excel with an amazing team to support you. You will have the opportunity to support audit activities for the Company’s technology and product functions (e.g., Business Technology, Engineering, Product Management), with a growing focus on how AI and agentic capabilities are adopted, governed, and controlled across these functions. What You'll Actually Be Doing Success will be measured upon the Auditor successfully executing key tasks, including: Support audits that assess risks and controls over AI and agentic capabilities
